expl.summary: Each jet (its 8 hardest particles) is placed on 16 neurons, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each of the five class scores adds some neurons and subtracts others; the formula's accuracy on the validation jets is 0.653. The t score is built mainly on λ₁+λ₂: it subtracts neuron 13 (ΣzΔR below 0.148 and λ₁ below 0.0164; true tops average 1.08 on it, every other class 3.6-4.5; -48% of the t score) and adds neuron 10 (overall λ₁+λ₂: ΣzΔR, ΣzΔR², λ₁; +26%), so it follows ΣzΔR and λ₁+λ₂ with rank correlations of 0.917 and 0.913. The q score is mostly neuron 9 (narrow, centred jets, +56%) minus neuron 10 (λ₁+λ₂, -18%), and follows jet mass and λ₁ downwards (rank correlations -0.765 and -0.763). The g score also adds neuron 9 (+22%), and in addition the low-mass, low-angularity neuron 2 (+38%, its largest input) and the broad, small-mass/pT, high-pT neuron 1 (+13%); it subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the hardest particles, -14%), which is how gluons are separated from quarks. The two boson scores share the elongated, mass/pT-window neuron 7 (+13% of W, +35% of Z) and subtract wide-angle radiation (neuron 3: -16% of W, -23% of Z) and the broad, off-centre neuron 6 (-9% and -14%). They are split mainly by λ₁+λ₂: the W score adds the compact, centred neuron 11 (+23%) and neuron 0 (+10%), which the Z score does not use, and subtracts the intermediate-λ₁+λ₂ neuron 14 (-9%) and the moderate-λ₁+λ₂ neuron 15 (-7%), while the Z score adds neuron 14 (+6%). Of the particle-mass thresholds that were offered, only two are used, and in small terms: largest subjet-pair mass < 62.55 GeV (half the Higgs mass, neuron 2) and mass > 91.19 GeV (the Z mass, neuron 12); since the jet mass here is that of the 8 hardest particles and does not peak at the W, Z or top masses, these act as ordinary mass cuts.

It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ and falls with planar flow, N₂ and τ₂₁ (rank correlations 0.561, -0.561, -0.554, -0.546). W (2.02) and Z (1.98) jets sit highest, far above tops (0.37), gluons (0.15) and quarks (0.15); it is zero for 88.3% of gluons, 89.4% of quarks and 80.4% of tops, but only for 23.9% of W and 22.2% of Z jets.
0.role: It raises the W score (+10% of its average input) and lowers the g score (-6%). It does not enter the q, Z or t scores.

1.title: broad jet with small mass/pT and high total pT
1.measures: Pushed down for narrow jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.00868 is its strongest term, -11.4%, together with λ₁+λ₂ < 0.0061 and ΣzΔR < 0.102) and pushed up for small (mass/pT)² (< 0.00583, +9.7%) and for high total pT (log of total pT > 6.50 and > 6.38); the pT of the 5 hardest particles adds above 368 GeV but subtracts above 531 GeV, and e₃ < 0.000512 and λ₁ < 0.00595 add a little. It rises with angularity (Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½), ΣzΔR and the distance of the hardest particle from the axis (rank correlations 0.6, 0.596, 0.582). Tops (1.20) and Z jets (1.01) sit highest, gluons (0.73) and W (0.60) in the middle, quarks lowest (0.31); it is zero for 66.8% of quarks and 51.6% of gluons, but only for 15.1% of tops.
1.role: It raises the g score (+13%) and, a little, the Z score (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: low jet mass, low subjet-pair mass and small angularity
2.measures: Its strongest terms subtract for a soft 8th-hardest particle (pT_7 < 53.4 GeV, -12.6%) and for large angularity (Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.133, -10.5%), and add for mass/pT < 0.108 (+10.1%) and total pT < 813 GeV (+9.4%); a largest subjet-pair mass below 62.55 GeV (half the Higgs mass, one of the offered thresholds) adds +6.5%, while z₇ > 0.0363, very light jets (mass < 36.2 GeV) and max ΔR < 0.251 subtract. Overall it falls with the largest subjet-pair mass and the jet mass of the 8 particles (rank correlations -0.719 and -0.709) and rises with M₂ (0.684). Gluons sit highest (3.53), then quarks (2.56), well above W (1.56), Z (1.29) and tops (1.28); it is rarely zero (3.6% of gluons, 22.1% of Z jets).
2.role: It raises the g score, where it is the largest input (+38%). It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores.

3.title: large mass/pT with pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 and widely separated subjets

5.title: pT concentrated in the hardest particles, very narrow core

5.role: It raises the q score (+6%) and lowers the g score (-14%) and the t score (-15%). It does not enter the W or Z scores.
